latin_text: Augustine also asserted, as Gregory later confirmed, that there is no visible thing among us over which an angelic power does not preside, and that all bodies are constantly ruled by a rational spirit of life. Origen likewise, in his commentary on the book of Numbers, says that the world needs angels to preside over animals and their birth and also over the increase of bushes and plantings and other things.
english_translation: Augustine also asserted, as Gregory later confirmed, that there is no visible thing among us over which an angelic power does not preside, and that all bodies are constantly ruled by a rational spirit of life. Origen likewise, in his commentary on the book of Numbers, says that the world needs angels to preside over animals and their birth and also over the increase of bushes and plantings and other things.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico cites patristic authority (Augustine, Gregory, Origen) to establish that no created thing—animal, plant, or mineral—exists without angelic governance. Each creature is "ruled by a rational spirit of life." [INFERRED] This extends the ninefold correspondence: each of the nine angelic orders governs a corresponding level of terrestrial being and life-form. The hierarchy is complete and universal.

The philosophical function is to ground natural magic and angelology: understanding creation means understanding the angelic orders that govern it. Conversely, practicing virtue means aligning oneself with an angelic order and participating in its governance. [INFERRED] This justifies both contemplative mysticism (ascending to angelic intellection) and active engagement with nature (governing as the angels govern).

[INFERRED] Oration (O.1.15) describes the three archangels as guides through the philosophical disciplines (ethics, physics, theology)—each angelic guide governs a domain. Being & Unity grounds it: angelic governance is participated divine causality.
